subject.title: Text between tool calls leaks to messaging channels

question: Should OpenClaw keep automatic bare-text source replies as the default for channel turns, or move tool-using/phase-less channel delivery toward final-only or message-tool-owned semantics across interactive and cron paths?
rationale: The secure UX fix conflicts with existing compatibility expectations for deployments that rely on automatic plain assistant replies, and repository policy treats channel delivery, fallback behavior, and config/default changes as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Adopt central final-only/tool-owned semantics
options.body: Make the shared payload/source-delivery boundary suppress intermediate phase-less segments for tool-using channel turns, with tests for interactive and cron delivery plus documented upgrade behavior.

options.title: Add a narrow opt-in delivery flag
options.body: Introduce a default-off final-only or last-segment-only channel/account setting for operators on phase-less transports, accepting that the unsafe default remains until a later migration.

options.title: Keep automatic delivery and document workarounds
options.body: Leave current behavior in place and steer users to `message_tool_only`, prompts, or streaming settings, accepting continued leak risk for existing channel workflows.

recommendation.title: Adopt central final-only/tool-owned semantics
recommendation.body: Make the shared payload/source-delivery boundary suppress intermediate phase-less segments for tool-using channel turns, with tests for interactive and cron delivery plus documented upgrade behavior.
